title: Platform systems & services: playbook, runbooks, dashboards and roadmap (Q3 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is the canonical playbook for Redwood Inference's platform team: a consolidated reference covering systems & services inventory, operational how-tos, dashboard and alert definitions, canonical runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the roadmap for Q3 2026. It is intended for platform engineers, on-call SREs, service owners, and engineering managers.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-recovery for platform incidents by standardizing runbooks and alerts.
- Provide a single, searchable inventory of platform services and owners.
- Align dashboards and SLOs to customer-facing SLAs and internal reliability targets.
- Publish a clear roadmap for observability and runbook improvements for Q3 2026.

Owners and contacts:
- Platform lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.example.com)
- On-call Slack: #platform-oncall
- Pager: Platform rotation (primary -> secondary) via PagerDuty
- Escalation path: oncall -> Platform EM -> Head of SRE (Daniel Kim) -> CTO

Systems & services inventory (summary):
| Service name | Owner | Primary purpose | Core SLOs | Key dashboards |
|-------------|-------|-----------------|----------|----------------|
| edge-gateway | eng-platform (team) | Ingress, auth, rate limiting | Availability 99.95% | Platform Overview, Edge Gateway - Errors |
| api-proxy | svc-api-team | API routing and aggregation | P99 latency < 200ms | API - Latency & Errors |
| model-router | eng-serving-runtime | Route inference requests to runtime pools | Throughput SLO: 95% of requests served without retry | Serving Runtime - Latency & KV Cache |
| kv-cache | eng-platform | Prefix and KV caching for token reuse | Cache hit-rate >= 65% for production traffic | KV Cache - Hit Rate & Utilization |
| gpu-fleet | eng-infra | GPU fleet and node autoscaling | Capacity target: < 5% tail capacity shortages | GPU Fleet - Utilization & Node Health |

How-tos (quick procedures):

1) Deploying a small platform service (canary -> rollout):
   1. Validate CI build: ensure green unit tests and integration tests.
   2. Create canary release in staging cluster: kubectl apply -f release-canary.yaml --namespace staging.
   3. Run smoke checks (curl health endpoints, run synthetic traffic for 10 minutes).
   4. Promote to production canary 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Monitor the following dashboards: Platform Overview, Service-specific latency & error panels.
   5. If no regressions, increment traffic 25% for 15 minutes, then 50%, then 100%. Document rollout in the release ticket.

2) Adding a new Prometheus metric & dashboard panel:
   - Instrumentation: add metric with stable name and labels using client_golang; follow metric naming guidelines (service_component_event_total).
   - Create or update Grafana dashboard JSON in repo infra/observability/dashboards. Commit PR and request observability reviewer.
   - Add alert rule to prometheus/rules/service.rules.yml and include runbook link.

Dashboards & alerts (canonical definitions):

Primary dashboards (Grafana):
- Platform Overview - key health metrics (global error rate, request rate, latency percentiles, cost delta).
- Serving Runtime - Latency & KV Cache - p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit-rate, inflight requests.
- GPU Fleet - Utilization - GPU utilization by pool, node allocation, queued jobs.
- API - Latency & Errors - per-route p95/p99, error rates, upstream latencies.

Alerting guide (thresholds & intent):
- Sev 1 (page oncall):
  - Platform Overview: global error rate > 1% for 5m AND error count > 100/min.
  - API p99 latency > 1s sustained for 5m for production routes.
  - GPU Fleet: queued requests > 1000 and autoscaler failing to scale nodes for 10m.
- Sev 2 (notify oncall, possibly page if escalated):
  - Service-specific error rate > 0.5% for 10m.
  - KV Cache hit-rate drop > 10 percentage points from baseline for 5m.
- Sev 3 (ticket):
  - Minor dashboard regression (single route latency spike for < 15m).

Alert ownership and runbook linking requirement: every alert must include a runbook_url label that points to the canonical runbook (see Runbooks section).

Runbooks (canonical templates and examples):
- Runbook naming: runbook-<service>-<primary-failure-mode>.md and stored in eng-platform/runbooks/.
- Minimum runbook sections: summary, impact, detection, immediate mitigation steps, deep-dive steps, rollback steps, postmortem checklist, owners, related dashboards.

Example runbook excerpt: API proxy - increased 5xx errors
1. Triage: check Platform Overview and API - Latency & Errors for correlated spikes.
2. Immediate mitigation:
   - If 5xx rate > 1%: scale api-proxy replicas by 2x: kubectl scale deploy api-proxy --replicas=<current*2> --namespace prod.
   - If scaling fails or errors persist: route traffic to fallback cluster (runbook: traffic-failover).
3. Deep dive: collect logs (kubectl logs -l app=api-proxy --since=10m), check recent deploys, inspect upstream service latencies.
4. Post-incident: create an incident ticket, run incident review, action items into roadmap if needed.

Retrospectives (recent learnings):
- Q2 2026 incident (GPU autoscaler regression): root cause was misconfigured scale policy combined with an abrupt model onboarding burst. Remediations implemented: tighter autoscaler testing in CI, synthetic load tests during canary, and a new pre-scale buffer for model-onboard events.
- Observability gaps identified: insufficient KV cache visibility for long-tail prefixes. Roadmap items below address this.

Roadmap (Q3 2026 priorities and milestones):
- Observability improvements (owner: Sofia Martinez, ETA: 2026-06-30):
  - Add per-prefix KV cache metrics, reduce cardinality through bucketing, and add heatmaps to Grafana.
- Runbook modernization (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-07-15):
  - Convert legacy runbooks to the canonical template, add runbook linking to all current alerts.
- Alert tuning sprint (owner: eng-sre, ETA: 2026-07-31):
  - Evaluate false-positive alerts, adjust thresholds, and add smarter suppression during deploys.
- GPU fleet reliability (owner: eng-infra, ETA: 2026-08-15):
  - Implement contingency pools and autoscaler policy changes.

Operational policies & guardrails (short):
- All production dashboards must have corresponding alerts with runbooks.
- No unreviewed alert rule may be merged to main: changes require observability review + oncall sign-off.
- Rollouts > 20% traffic must include a deploy plan documented in the release ticket and a rollback threshold.

Appendix A - Quick CLI snippets:
- Check KV cache hit-rate (Prometheus query): sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Force scale api-proxy: kubectl scale deploy api-proxy --replicas=10 --namespace prod
- Restart model-router pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-router --namespace prod

Appendix B - Useful links:
- Platform team wiki: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example.com/d/platform-overview
- Runbooks repo: git@git.redwood.example.com:infra/observability-runbooks.git

- 2026-03-10: added GPU autoscaler retrospectives and mitigations.
- 2026-03-15: finalized dashboard thresholds and published (reviewers: Daniel Kim, Sofia Martinez).

If you are oncall and this document is missing crucial steps, update the runbook in eng-platform/runbooks and ping the platform lead for a review.
